title: The canonical closed-immersion cohomology comparison for units is bijective
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every $p\in\mathbb N$, the particular canonical homomorphism $c_i^p:H^p(X,i_*\mathcal O_Z^\times)\to H^p(Z,\mathcal O_Z^\times)$ defined by inverse image on Ext, the constant-integer-sheaf identification, and the counit in [def-sc-zariski-units-restriction] is bijective. Here cohomology is that of abelian Zariski sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology, def-sc-zariski-site].

source.place: Tag 02UV, cohomology-lemma-cohomology-and-closed-immersions, proof via exact direct image; canonical map identified using the source library Ext-adjunction theorem

proof.text: Direct image along the closed embedding preserves epimorphisms. Explicitly, an on-image local lift over V extends to the ambient open U minus i(Z minus V); off the image, the inverse-image open is empty. The local-surjectivity criterion proves preservation of epimorphisms. Direct image is additive and left exact, so it is exact. Inverse image is additive and exact as well.

Apply the source library Ext-adjunction theorem CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mapExtCounit_bijective to the exact inverse-image/direct-image adjunction, the constant integer sheaf on X, and the units sheaf on Z. It says that applying inverse image to an Ext class and then composing with the counit is bijective. Precomposition by the constant-sheaf pullback isomorphism is an additive equivalence. Associativity of Ext composition identifies their composite with exactly c_i^p of def-sc-zariski-units-restriction. Thus this canonical map is bijective, without choosing an unspecified cohomology isomorphism.
